title: Plaque Assay for Phage Lambda
author: Marijn Ceelen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7i8hkhw

steps.title: Prepare E. coli Culture
steps.instruction: Prepare a susceptible E. coli strain (e.g., LE392 or DH10B) for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Streak E. coli on an LB plate and incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Pick a single colony and inoculate 10 mL of LB.
Incubate the culture at 37 °C until the OD reaches 2-3 (overnight culture is recommended).

steps.title: Infect E. coli with Phage
steps.instruction: Mix phage dilutions with the bacterial culture to allow infection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a range of phage dilutions.
Mix 100 µL of phage dilution with 200 µL of E. coli culture.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Add Soft Agar and Plate
steps.instruction: Combine the infected culture with soft agar and pour onto LB plates.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 mL of liquid soft LB agar (0.7% agar) maintained at 50 °C to the mixture.
Pour the resulting mixture onto LB plates that have been preheated to 37 °C.
Spread the mixture by moving the plate, working quickly to prevent agar clumps.

steps.title: Incubate Plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates to allow plaque formation.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the plates for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Turn the plates over and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Calculate Phage Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the Plaque Forming Units (PFU)/mL using plates containing 30-300 plaques.

substeps.instruction: Count the number of plaques of lysis (N).
Calculate PFU/mL using the formula: PFU/mL = N × 1/DF × 1/V, where DF is the dilution factor and V is the volume of phage dilution poured on the plate.
